title: Philippians
summary: Philippians is a biblical book focused on Christlike humility, partnership, joy, perseverance, gospel witness, and resurrection hope.
historical_context: Philippians encourages gospel partnership and Christ-shaped humility amid pressure and hope.
ancient_near_east_context: Philippians belongs to the ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern world reflected in its setting, institutions, and canonical placement.
hebraic_worldview: Philippians should be read with attention to covenant memory, communal identity, worship, wisdom, and accountability before the Lord.
second_temple_context: Second Temple readers received Philippians as part of Israel's Scriptures and read it within questions of identity, worship, exile, and hope.
canonical_context: Within Pauline Epistles, book 6 of 13, Philippians contributes to the Bible's unfolding witness by connecting Christlike humility, partnership, joy, perseverance, gospel witness, and resurrection hope to the larger storyline.
later_christian_reception: Christian interpretation has read Philippians as part of the canonical witness to faithfulness, judgment, mercy, and hope in Christ-centered Scripture reading.
literary_context: Philippians uses epistle within Pauline Epistles, book 6 of 13 to develop its themes through the book's structure and key passages.
covenantal_significance: Philippians helps readers trace covenant faithfulness, failure, mercy, and hope within its canonical setting.
authorship_positions: Traditional Pauline authorship or Pauline circle attribution
Critical scholarship debates several letters and recognizes co-workers in some correspondence
date_ranges: Some disputed letters are placed later or in the Pauline school
original_audience: Mixed Jewish-Gentile congregations and church leaders across the Roman world
historical_setting: The Greco-Roman world of mission, patronage, and local house churches
canonical_role: Philippians anchors Christlike humility, partnership, joy, perseverance, gospel witness, and resurrection hope within Pauline Epistles, book 6 of 13 and connects the book to related people, places, events, and themes.
interpretive_disputes: How doctrine, ethics, and pastoral counsel fit together

related_objects.notes: Paul writes as missionary partner and pastor.
The Christ hymn is a major theological anchor.
The church is called to stand firm.

interpretive_notes.note: Read Philippians first within its own literary setting before moving to broader canonical connections.
